# Build decisions

Decisions made during the build, recorded so later work and reviewers can see why the implementation differs from, or adds to, the [numbered specifications](../notes/files/00_index.md). Deployment-specific values (addresses, secrets, account IDs) are kept in an untracked local file, not here.

Status: **Confirmed** by the owner, or **Build default** chosen during implementation and open to change.

## Scope additions and changes

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | **Quick chat**: temporary Simon conversations not attached to a task. Floating button at the bottom right, shown only when no task is selected; the panel opens out of the button; full screen on mobile. Ending the chat deletes it; unattended chats expire after 24 hours; "Save as task" turns it into a task that keeps the conversation. Simon acts as a workspace helper (find/open/create/move tasks, reminders, drafting, approved connector actions, handoff prompts) and can read but not edit a named task. No Vault or incoming MCP access; not searchable. | Confirmed | New note 18 and screen brief |
| D2 | **Six themes**: Studio, Paper, Pebble, Postcard, Meadow and Tide from the UI sample, each usable with any accent and Light/Dark/System. | Confirmed | Note 02 and themes brief (four themes) |
| D3 | **Reminders are due-date notices, not alarms**: delivered at the top of the hour in the user's local time. The scanner wakes at :00, :15 and :30 past each UTC hour, which gives every current IANA zone its local top of the hour (covers +5:30, +5:45, +8:45, +12:45/+13:45, −3:30 and −9:30; no zone needs :45). Reminder times are whole hours; relative reminders round down; snooze offers 1 hour, Tomorrow at 9 and a custom hour. | Confirmed (timing); build default (mechanism, choices) | Note 15 (60 s polling, 15-minute snooze) |
| D4 | **Incoming MCP** at `/mcp` on the API origin, authenticated by **OAuth 2.1** (with an in-app consent screen) and by **bearer API keys**. | Confirmed | Agent connections brief (auth pending) |
| D5 | **Analytics on, with a mandatory cookie consent banner**. Nothing loads or is stored before Accept; Decline is as easy as Accept; the choice syncs with Settings → Account → Privacy. The banner appears after sign-in because login, Vault and share routes never load analytics. PostHog US cloud. | Confirmed | Note 17 (settings-only opt-in) |
| D6 | **All Composio connectors** are offered, fetched live from Composio on demand and not stored. Auth configs are looked up or created automatically. Connectors that cannot use shared credentials are hidden unless the user can supply their own API key through Composio's hosted form. | Confirmed (catalogue); build default (hiding) | Onboarding/connections briefs (sample catalogue) |
| D7 | **Composio-managed shared OAuth** until a business case is proven. Switching to own OAuth apps later requires affected users to reconnect, surfaced as Needs attention. | Confirmed | Note 12 |
| D8 | **AI providers**: OpenAI by default (Fast `gpt-5.6-luna`, Smart `gpt-5.6-terra`, verified on OpenAI's model pages on 2026-09-15). Provider registry also supports Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic), Google Vertex AI and Together AI. OpenAI programmatic tool calling (hosted code runtime) is never enabled. AI operational telemetry is on (no content). | Confirmed | Note 07 |

## Architecture and operations

| # | Decision | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | `DURABLE=true` in hosted environments. Local development without a Trigger secret key falls back to the Nest executor, which the spec already supports. | Confirmed |
| A2 | Hosting: Next.js on Vercel, NestJS on Render (single always-on instance), Trigger.dev Cloud. Merges to `main` auto-deploy all three. Vercel previews run without a backend until a separate dev backend exists, so previews never reach production. | Confirmed (hosting, auto-deploy); build default (previews) |
| A3 | Trigger machines: **micro** for most tasks including chat runs; **small-1x** for Git document tasks. On out-of-memory, idempotent background tasks retry on a larger machine; chat runs are marked interrupted with an explicit Retry, never re-run automatically. | Confirmed (sizes); build default (OOM handling) |
| A4 | Master keys (`CONTENT_KEK`, `VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY`) come from environment variables behind a key-provider interface so a KMS can be enabled later without code changes. | Confirmed |
| A5 | Runtime and tooling verified 2026-09-15: Node.js 24 LTS (24.21.0 current; `engines` >=24.15), pnpm 12.4.2, Trigger.dev 4.6.0 (`runtime: "node-24"`, Git via `aptGet`). Remaining stack versions are recorded in [progress](progress.md) as they are verified. | Build default |
| A6 | pnpm 12 supply-chain policy is kept: dependency build scripts are allowed only for listed packages, and deliberately pinned releases newer than the minimum release age are listed explicitly in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. | Build default |
| A7 | **Local development adapters**: without Cloudflare/Resend/AI credentials the app runs locally with clearly labeled development adapters (SQLite file standing in for D1 with the same batch semantics, filesystem standing in for R2, OTP emails printed to the server log). They are refused when `NODE_ENV=production`. Production uses D1 REST and R2 only. | Build default |
| A8 | Every feature ships with tests. Integrations are tested against stand-ins that model documented provider behavior, plus separately labeled live checks that run only when credentials are present. | Confirmed |

## Architecture review 1 rulings

Build defaults recorded when architecture review 1 (`docs/build/reviews/architecture-review-1.md`) was applied to the [architecture](architecture.md). Each row changes or interprets a specification.

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | **Vault unlock runs server-side.** The api derives the passphrase key with Argon2id and issues a `__Host-sym_vault` session bound to the user and login session (5 minutes idle, 60 minutes absolute). The passphrase exists only in request memory: never logged, never in error reports or idempotency records. Unlock allows 5 failures per 15 minutes then a 15-minute lockout, and 20 per 24 hours, counted in D1. Simon grants name one item, task, tool slug and argument path, last at most 24 hours, and resolved values are redacted from results. | Build default | Note 05 ("unlock locally", "regular vault decryption can remain in the browser") |
| R2 | **Encrypted worker-to-api push is the only durable output path.** The worker posts signed, encrypted chunk envelopes to the api. No Trigger realtime streams, `chat.agent`, `AgentChat` or transcript storage, no `@ai-sdk/otel` (`TRIGGER_AI_SDK_OTEL_AUTOREGISTER=0`, AI SDK telemetry off), a redacting worker logger, and ids-only Trigger payloads, metadata, outputs and tags, verified by a marker-string test. | Build default | Note 07 (Trigger session output consumed by Nest); Trigger research recommendations for `chat.agent` and streams |
| R3 | **D1 budget allocation and a dedicated worker token.** All runtimes together stay at or below 3 requests per second: api 2 req/s (burst 10, unauthenticated work at most 30%), worker at most 1 req/s in total through its own D1 token, a bounded D1 queue family and per-process token buckets. Any 429 opens a process-wide circuit for Retry-After (default 300 s). The live suite must confirm whether Cloudflare limits apply per token, user or account; the owner should request a limit increase before a wider beta. | Build default | Note 07 gap 2 (handle rate limits); Cloudflare research R1 |
| R4 | **Symplist-owned single-approval pauses.** `parallelToolCalls: false`; an `execute_tools` call holds either only approval-exempt actions or exactly one approval-requiring action, so each pause has one approval. Decisions are approve (optionally with edited arguments that create a fresh review and digest), deny or dismiss, each applied by one owner-bound conditional statement so exactly one decision per approval takes effect; denial, dismissal and time-based or connection-change expiry go back to the model in a continuation, while restriction and task archive stop the paused run without one. A pending approval or question keeps the conversation active for queueing, and a chat reply is never an approval. The approval policy is deterministic. | Build default | Note 12 (per-action approval inside batches); AI SDK research (SDK `toolApproval`) |
| R5 | **Per-user Composio session** pinned to connected accounts confirmed through a Symplist connection attempt (nonce, same login session, callback identity verification). `manage_connections` is a native Symplist tool that never calls `COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS`. | Build default | Note 12 (`manage_connections` mapping); Composio research (session per chat) |
| R6 | **Git runs in a `document-git` task** (small-1x, awaited by the chat run) in durable mode and in process locally; it never runs inside the chat run. Every publication writes an immutable encrypted head snapshot, which serves outline, section reads, changes, search indexing and artifact snapshots. | Build default | Note 11 (runtime and Git operations); A3 |
| R7 | **Editor formatting normalization and section-level view switching.** The first page-view edit of a non-canonical document publishes a separate "Formatting normalized" commit treated as content-neutral; documents with raw HTML open read-only in the page view; switching between page and raw views preserves the section, not the character position. | Build default | Note 11 (autosave); task document brief ("switching views preserves content and position") |
| R8 | **Proceeding without live D1 verification.** The owner instructed the build not to wait for Cloudflare credentials, so feature waves build against conservative local semantics (string params, same-batch verification `SELECT`, `STRICT` tables). The live D1 suite runs as soon as credentials exist and any divergence is fixed before beta. | Build default | Note 04 (demonstrate atomic REST design); research requirement to verify before building |
| R9 | **`analytics_id` and consent state are plaintext operational metadata.** The id is random and never exposed in responses or logs; server emitters read it without decryption, and account purge must read it after the account key is shredded. | Build default | Note 17 ("account-side protected mapping") |
| R10 | **Expand-only migrations with a CI `migrate` job** that runs before the Trigger deploy; Render pre-deploy runs the same idempotent runner as a safety net. Contract changes ship a release later, and merged migration files never change. | Build default | Hosting decision A2 (independent auto-deploys) |
| R11 | **One-time secrets are never replayable.** Invite codes, API keys, share tokens and OAuth codes appear only in the minting response; idempotency records keep a redacted outcome, and retries return `secretUnavailable: true` with a revoke-and-replace path. | Build default | Notes 04 and 16 (show once) |
| R12 | **Account deletion is an immediate crypto-shred** (deleting the account key row in the same batch as the restriction), followed by an idempotent purge of Composio accounts (revoked upstream), R2 objects, D1 rows and PostHog data. Residual window: D1 Time Travel retains prior states for 30 days; R2 is unversioned; Trigger holds no content (decision R2); PostHog deletion is asynchronous. | Build default | P4; settings account brief (deletion process) |
| R13 | **Admin bootstrap runs once**, only while no admin and no bootstrap event exist, and never clears suspension or relock; re-bootstrapping needs an explicit forced CLI run with actor and reason. | Build default | Note 04 (bootstrap first administrator) |
| R14 | **Resend delivery webhooks are optional.** The webhook is implemented and recommended, but `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not required: without it the endpoint returns 404, deliveries stop at `accepted`, bounce/complaint suppression is off, and the bounced-address settings state is hidden (architecture §12.5). | Confirmed | Note 15 (permanent failure suppression) |

## Foundation build defaults

Decisions made while building the foundation (Phase C) against the [architecture](architecture.md), each verified in the repository on 2026-09-15.

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | **Relative imports use `.ts` specifiers.** `tsconfig.base.json` sets `allowImportingTsExtensions` and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`, so `tsc -b` emits `.js` specifiers in `dist` while Turbopack, Vitest and the Trigger bundler read sources directly. Turbopack in Next 16.3.5 cannot resolve NodeNext `.js` specifiers to `.ts` files (a `next build` importing `@symplist/contracts` through `turbopack.resolveAlias` failed with 52 "Module not found" errors). A structural test rejects `.js` relative specifiers in `packages/*/src` and `apps/api/src`. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (6) |
| F2 | **Vitest resolves `@symplist/*` through a resolver plugin, not `resolve.conditions`.** The shared config maps each workspace specifier to its package's `source` export. Vitest forwards `ssr.resolve.conditions` to test workers as Node `--conditions` flags, and third-party packages also publish a `source` export (for example `eventsource`, loaded by `@trigger.dev/core`) that points at TypeScript files Node refuses to load from `node_modules`, so a test importing `queue` from `@trigger.dev/sdk` crashed with the conditions approach. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (4) |
| F3 | **`vitest.config.ts` files import the shared config by relative path** (`packages/testing/src/vitest-config.ts`). Vite's config loader resolves bare imports with only the `node` condition, so importing `@symplist/testing/vitest` there would require a built `dist`. `@symplist/testing` depends on the packages whose interfaces its fakes and contract suites cover (config, contracts, crypto, db, email, storage); those packages never depend on it, so the workspace graph stays acyclic. Every other package and app lists it as a dev dependency. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (4), §17 |
| F4 | **Two tsconfigs per built project.** `tsconfig.json` is the composite build (tests excluded, `tsBuildInfoFile` inside `dist` so deleting `dist` gives a clean build); `tsconfig.typecheck.json` is the `noEmit` check with `customConditions: ["source"]` that includes tests and `vitest.config.ts`. The web typecheck runs `next typegen` first, and `next-env.d.ts` is not committed. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (1), (3) |
| F5 | **`pnpm build` runs `next build` before `tsc -b`**, so the CI build step is also the clean-clone web build smoke test (no package `dist` exists yet). `pnpm build:web:clean` removes `packages/*/dist` and builds the web app for the same check locally. A web test asserts that the Turbopack aliases are exactly the browser-safe entries and match each package's `source` export, and a static import scan in `packages/testing` keeps those entries free of `node:*` and server-only workspace imports. | Build default | Architecture §2 and §2.2 (6) |
| F6 | **Pins not spelled out in the stack lock:** `@tanstack/react-query` 5.102.8 (latest stable on 2026-09-15); `cn` 0.3.0 in `apps/web` (installed by `shadcn init` 4.21.0 and re-exported by its generated `lib/utils.ts`); `react-dom` 19.3.0 in `packages/email` (required peer of `react-email` and `@react-email/render`); `zod` 4.6.5 in the worker, agent, integrations and analytics packages (required peer of `@trigger.dev/sdk`, `ai` and `@composio/core`). `shadcn` is a web dependency as `init` makes it. It brings `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.0 in as its own transitive dependency, as the `trigger.dev` CLI already did; Symplist code never imports it (the MCP server uses the 2.0 packages). | Build default | Architecture §1 |
| F7 | **`core-js: false` in `allowBuilds`.** It arrives through `posthog-js`, and its postinstall only prints a funding message. | Build default | A6 |
| F8 | **Error-code maps map each code to its HTTP status**, declared per feature with `defineErrorCodes` and composed in the contracts index; a test fails if two owners declare the same code, event type or tool name. Common codes: `not_found` 404, `rate.limited` 503 and `idempotency.mismatch` 422 (the status the IETF Idempotency-Key draft uses for a reused key with a different payload). | Build default | Architecture §6, §6.1 |
| F9 | **`@symplist/core` exports one subpath per core domain** (`@symplist/core/access`, `@symplist/core/events`, …) and re-exports each domain as a namespace from its root, so domain builders never edit the manifest and names never collide. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (1), §2.3 |
| F10 | **Nest decorator transform in tests is configured explicitly** (`oxc.decorator: { legacy: true, emitDecoratorMetadata: true }` in `apps/api/vitest.config.ts`), because Oxc takes these options from the tsconfig that includes a file and the build tsconfig excludes tests. The api test asserts `design:paramtypes` for `HealthController`. | Build default | Architecture §17 |
| C1.1 | **Ids accept only canonical lowercase UUIDv7 text**, branded per entity (`TaskId`, `RunId`, …) with `brandedIdSchema`, so one id never has two spellings in D1 rows, R2 keys or cache keys. Request ids stay opaque tokens (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`). | Build default | Architecture §3.4 |
| C1.2 | **Foundation error codes:** `validation` 400, `internal` 500, `auth.session_required` 401, `auth.origin_forbidden` and `auth.csrf_invalid` 403, `access.unverified`, `access.locked`, `access.relocked`, `access.suspended` and `access.admin_required` 403, `idempotency.key_required` and `idempotency.key_invalid` 400, `idempotency.in_progress` 409, `task.archived` and `task.run_active` 409, besides F8's codes. `rate.limited` carries `details.retryAfter` in whole seconds (1 to 86400); `validation` details carry path, code and a fixed message, never the input. `defineErrorCodes`, `defineEvents` and `defineTools` reject malformed names at import. | Build default | Architecture §6, §6.1; F8 |
| C1.3 | **One-time secret responses are a strict union on `secretUnavailable`:** the minting response carries the secret fields with `secretUnavailable: false`; an exact retry carries only the non-secret fields with `secretUnavailable: true` and `notice: "secret.already_issued"`, and can never carry a secret field. | Build default | Architecture §6.1; R11 |
| C1.4 | **WebSocket frame contracts:** user-topic events (the §7 list, each owned by one feature in `userTopicEventOwners`) travel only on `user`, every other event only on `conversation:<id>`; the composed decoder rejects unknown event types; malformed client frames are answered with `{"t":"err","code":"validation"}`. `openTasks` must be unique; the user snapshot's `heads` holds at most 20 opaque revisions. | Build default | Architecture §7 |
| C1.5 | **Environment parsing:** an empty value counts as unset; booleans accept only `true`/`false` and `LIVE_*` only `1`/`0`; integers must be canonical decimals; origins must be canonical (`scheme://host[:port]`, no path or trailing slash), including `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL`. `NODE_ENV` is required on the api and defaults to `production` on the worker (Trigger.dev images set `production`, `trigger dev` sets `development`), so `WorkerConfig` gains `NODE_ENV`. Defaults: `PORT` 4000, `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` 0 outside production, OTP 6 digits/10 minutes/5 attempts, Vault idle 5 minutes, lateness and quick-chat TTL 24 hours, `DOC_MAX_BYTES` 1 MiB (also the maximum, so an encrypted draft fits D1's 2 MB value limit), `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` UTC, `GIT_TMP_DIR` `<os tmpdir>/symplist-git`, AI tiers from D8, `AI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` true (D8), `BETA_ACCESS_REQUIRED`, reminders and AI true, analytics false. | Build default | Architecture §16.1, §16.2 |
| C1.6 | **Cross-field rules added to §16.1:** production also requires https/wss origins, `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` and `AI_PROVIDER_MODE=live` (scripted stays allowed in development and test); `WS_ORIGIN` must share `API_ORIGIN`'s host and port; `ARTIFACT_ORIGIN` must use a different hostname from `API_ORIGIN` and `WEB_ORIGIN`; the api needs `EMAIL_FROM_REMINDERS` when `DURABLE=false`; analytics with a project key needs `POSTHOG_HOST`, and on the api `POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID` so account deletion can delete PostHog data; Bedrock and Vertex credentials must be complete groups. Missing AI credentials never fail startup (`ai.unavailable`). | Build default | Architecture §5.6, §5.8, §13, §16.1 |
| C1.7 | **Secret inventory enforcement:** a "no" cell (`TRIGGER_ACCESS_TOKEN` on api and worker) is refused like "rejected"; with `DURABLE=true` the api refuses the secret AI credentials (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `GOOGLE_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS_JSON`, `TOGETHER_API_KEY`) but not region, project or location; the worker patterns also match unversioned names (`VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY`); an unversioned family name is refused in every runtime. The web config refuses every inventory secret and any `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` outside the four public names, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` must be a `phc_` project key; http/ws web URLs are allowed only for loopback hosts, because the e2e suite runs a production web build against a local api. | Build default | Architecture §4.5, §16.1 |
| C1.8 | **`syncEnvVars` source:** `workerSyncEnvVars(process.env)` from `@symplist/config/worker` selects only the allowlist (every worker variable except `NODE_ENV` and `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY`, plus the worker families' `<NAME>_<n>` and `<NAME>_CURRENT`), always syncs `TRIGGER_AI_SDK_OTEL_AUTOREGISTER=0`, marks provider credentials and family versions secret, and validates the selection with the worker schema before returning it, so a deploy fails instead of syncing an invalid or forbidden configuration. | Build default | Architecture §4.5, §8.8 |
| C1.9 | **`pnpm secrets:generate` imports the inventory** from `packages/config/src/secrets.ts` through Node 24 type stripping (the file is dependency-free and uses only erasable syntax), prints shared families first and api-only families under a separate heading, takes no arguments and never writes files. The browser-safe scan also fails entries that reach `posthog-node`, `@aws-sdk/*`, `@composio/core`, `resend`, `@nestjs/*`, `@trigger.dev/*`, the MCP server packages, Express middleware and the AI SDK provider packages. | Build default | Architecture §2, §16.3 |
| CR1 | **Envelope key versions are data key versions.** The `<keyVersion>` of `sym1` envelopes, the object header `kv` and the AAD `k` name the version of the data key that encrypted them (the account data key, or the Vault data key for items). Each account and Vault has one data key, so every envelope in this format generation carries `1`, and decryption rejects any other version with `crypto.unsupported_key_version` before touching the ciphertext (so the version is never malleable, even in the Vault item and grant AADs that omit `k`). `CONTENT_KEK` rotation unwraps the account key with its recorded KEK version and re-wraps it under the current one (`rewrapAccountKey`); envelopes are never re-encrypted. A later data-key rotation adds versions without changing the formats. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §4.2 |
| CR2 | **Key wrap and object layout details.** Every `symk1` wrap (account key, Vault passphrase, recovery and session) and the object `wk` is base64url of 12-byte IV, 32-byte encrypted key and 16-byte tag (80 characters). The per-object key is wrapped by the account data key under the same object AAD as the body (different keys). The object header is canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) `{"alg":"A256GCM","iv","kv","v","wk"}` after `SYMO`, version byte `1` and a big-endian uint32 header length; `v` is the object format version from the caller, and non-canonical headers are rejected. HKDF-SHA256 uses an empty salt and only the five fixed labels; the Vault session HKDF input is the token's 32 raw bytes. Random bytes are drawn in a fixed order (data key or object key, then wrap IV, then body IV) so the committed vectors in `packages/crypto/test-vectors/v1.json` are reproducible. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §11.1 |
| CR3 | **AAD encoder rules and the run chunk and idempotency bindings.** AAD field names are `a`–`z`; values are non-empty strings of at most 1,024 UTF-16 units without lone surrogates (escaped exactly as `JSON.stringify` does) or non-negative safe integers; `f` must be `sym1`, `symo1` or `symk1` and `p` is required. Run chunks bind purpose `run_chunk`, table `runs`, row = run id, column `seq:<seq>`. Idempotency responses bind purpose `idempotency_response`, owner = the record's user, table `idempotency_records`, row = canonical JSON `[scope, key]` (unambiguous when either contains separators) and column `response_enc`. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §4.2, §6.1 |
| CR4 | **Crypto size limits.** Field (`sym1`) plaintext at most 1 MiB, so an envelope stays under D1's 2 MB value limit; object plaintext at most 256 MiB; object header at most 1 KiB; digest input at most 16 MiB; Argon2id secrets at most 4 KiB of UTF-8. Tokens are 16 to 1,024 bytes (32 by default); OTPs are 6 to 12 digits drawn with one uniform `crypto.randomInt` call. Oversized input fails with `crypto.input_too_large`. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §5.1 |
| CR5 | **Digest value encodings.** Each §4.3 purpose is accepted only with its own secret family. The OTP digest value is canonical JSON `[challengeId, purpose, code]`. Idempotency fingerprints and approval argument digests hash canonical JSON (keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no whitespace, `JSON.stringify` scalars, `undefined` object members omitted; non-finite numbers, lone surrogates and non-plain objects rejected); the approval value is `{arguments, connectedAccountId, toolSlug}` and its digest is a bare base64url string because `approvals.arg_digest` stores no version. `email-suppression` digests carry the `CONTENT_KEK` version. A stored digest whose secret version is no longer configured verifies false. Internal event signatures (§6.2) are built by their owner from the exported `hmacSha256` and `constantTimeEqual`. | Build default | Architecture §4.3, §5.1, §6.1, §8.4 |
| CR6 | **Argon2id records and normalization.** Stored records must match the single supported parameter set exactly (`v` 1, `argon2id`, m=19456, t=2, p=1, 16-byte salt, 32-byte hash); anything else fails with `crypto.invalid_password_hash` before any work, so stored data can neither weaken nor inflate the cost. Secrets are NFKC-normalized before hashing (NIST SP 800-63B), so composed and decomposed input verify alike. Vault key derivation takes a salt-and-parameters record without `hash` (the foundation stub accepted `Argon2idHash`, which would have stored the wrapping key beside the wrap). A full semaphore refuses with `rate.limited` and `retryAfter` 1 second. | Build default | Architecture §4.3, §11.1, §13.3 |
| CR7 | **Environment key provider.** A family with no `<NAME>_<n>` or `<NAME>_CURRENT` variables is absent (callers list required families); versions must be canonical positive integers up to 999,999,999; values must be exactly 32 bytes of canonical unpadded base64url; `all()` lists versions newest first by number. Errors name the variable but never echo its value, and `destroy()` zeroises every key buffer. Cross-family equality and per-runtime rejection stay in `@symplist/config` (§4.5). | Build default | Architecture §4.5, decision A4 |
| C3-1 | **Query helper strictness.** `sql(text, params)` accepts only strings, `null`/`undefined` (written as `NULL` literals) and string arrays (expanded to `?, ?` lists; an empty array becomes the empty subquery `SELECT NULL WHERE 0`, so `IN (:ids)` matches no row and `NOT IN (:ids)` matches every row, where `NULL` would make `NOT IN` match nothing). Numbers and booleans must go through `int()`/`bool()`; unused or missing names throw. Both clients reject non-string params, placeholder-count mismatches, named or numbered placeholders, transaction control and multi-statement entries before any request. Errors carry stable codes; SQLite/D1 text is kept only in a non-enumerable `providerMessage`. | Build default | Architecture §3.2 |
| C3-2 | **D1 lane mechanics.** The api lane is a 10-token bucket at 2 req/s; unauthenticated calls also draw from a 3-token sub-bucket at 0.6 req/s, never queue, and are shed with `rate.limited` whenever tokens are short or authenticated work is waiting. Authenticated calls queue FIFO and are refused when the wait would exceed 5 s (api) or 120 s (worker). Clients share one process-wide lane per kind and one process-wide circuit; the circuit also opens until reset when a `Ratelimit` policy reports 10 or fewer requests remaining. Read-only batches retry up to 3 attempts (200 ms base, full jitter, 2 s cap) on retryable D1 messages, 5xx, network errors and malformed success bodies; timeouts are not retried. | Build default | Architecture §3.1 |

The seams `REALTIME_ACCESS_NOTIFIER`, `RUN_CANCELLER`, `REALTIME_SHUTDOWN` and `TRIGGER_CLIENT` are string tokens in `apps/api/src/common/seams.ts`, injected optionally and bound by the realtime and executor modules through a global provider; startup logs `platform.seam_unbound` for each missing one. | Build default | Architecture §5.5, §7, §8.1 |
| C6.10 | **Email normalization and the api test harness.** `normalizeEmail` trims, applies NFC, lowercases and applies NFC again (idempotent), and `emailAddressSchema` validates the normalized value with Zod's ASCII email rule. `apps/api/test/harness.ts` (`bootTestApp`) is the shared api test harness; probe controllers that use parameter decorators live in `apps/api/test/probes/` because the Biome override for `*.test.ts` does not enable `unsafeParameterDecoratorsEnabled`. The api `tsconfig.typecheck.json` includes `test` and adds `jsx` and the DOM lib so the email and analytics sources typecheck under the `source` condition, and `vitest.config.ts` includes `test/**/*.test.ts`. | Build default | Architecture §4.3, §5.1, §17 |
| C6.11 | **Unknown session cookies are limited per client network before D1.** A well-formed session cookie that misses both caches costs one D1 read, so an unauthenticated client inventing tokens could spend the whole api lane (§3.1). `SessionService.resolve` checks the in-memory `session_unknown` failure bucket (60 lookups per client network per 10 minutes) before a cache-missing lookup, and `SessionStore.lookup` tells ended sessions (revoked or expired) apart from tokens that name no session, so only the latter are recorded; over the bucket the api refuses with 503 `rate.limited`. Sessions already in the 10-second cache are never refused, and browsers holding the cookie of an ended session never fill the bucket. `resolveToken` (WebSocket upgrades, which have no Express `req.ip`) leaves the per-client limit to its caller. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §3.3, §5.8 |
| C6.12 | **Platform review amendments.** Account key provisioning writes only while `deletion_state = 'none'`, so no key can exist after the crypto-shred, and the account purge contributor also deletes any leftover `account_keys` row. Deletion statement 1 also requires `email` to equal the address the tombstone digest was computed from. `SessionRevokeInput` carries the deciding guard when revocation is folded into the deletion batch, and every contributed statement must include it. An exact retry of a `@OneTimeSecret` endpoint replays status 200 with the redacted outcome (§6.1); other replays keep the recorded status. Fingerprints include the raw body, query or params of any source a handler declares no argument for. `IdempotencyStore.complete` reuses the account key row read by the claiming batch (one D1 request). A local restriction records a generation floor and a local revocation a revoked-session marker for 60 seconds, so a session read in flight during the commit is not cached afterwards. Route-class credential stripping also removes `Cookie` and `Authorization` from `req.rawHeaders`. During shutdown the coordinator closes idle HTTP connections every 100 ms, so keep-alive connections end once their in-flight response finished instead of delaying the drain. | Build default | Architecture §3.3, §5.5, §5.6, §6.1, §7 |

## Realtime, internal endpoints and executors (Phase C-b, c7)

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C7.1 | **Internal signature format frozen.** `X-Sym-Timestamp` is Unix epoch **seconds** as a canonical decimal; `path` is the request target exactly as sent (Express `originalUrl`); `sha256(rawBody)` is 64 lower-case hex characters; the signature header is `v1=` plus 64 lower-case hex; timestamp, event id (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`), method (upper-case letters) and path (printable ASCII from `/`) are restricted so the 0x00 framing is unambiguous. `signInternalRequest`/`verifyInternalRequest` in `packages/crypto/src/internal-signature.ts` build it from `hmacSha256` and `constantTimeEqual` (CR5), check the ±300-second window and the `X-Sym-Key` version, and return typed failure reasons; frozen vectors live in `internal-signature.test.ts`. | Build default | Architecture §6.2; CR5 |
| C7.2 | **Internal request bodies use `application/vnd.symplist.internal+json`.** The api's global JSON parser ignores that media type, so the internal controllers read the exact raw bytes with their own limits (events 64 KiB, run output 2 MiB) instead of depending on `rawBody` and the 100 KB parser default. Every verification failure (malformed headers, stale timestamp, unknown key version, bad signature, replayed event id) and every ownership, status or generation rejection answers the same 404 `not_found`; a full replay memory (200,000 ids, fail closed) answers 503 `rate.limited`. A handler failure releases the event id so an identical retry is accepted. | Build default | Architecture §6, §6.2 |
| C7.3 | **Run output relay details.** Deduplication remembers the last 4,096 sequence numbers per run; ownership is cached until the run is rejected as unknown or idle for 15 minutes; status, the executor generation and the unwrapped account key are re-read at most every 10 seconds (keys are zeroised when dropped). Only `queued` and `running` runs relay. Each UI chunk is published as one `chunk` event with data `{runId, chunk}`; until Simon declares `chunk` in its contracts, the topic hub accepts that one undeclared type on conversation topics and rejects every other undeclared event. | Build default | Architecture §6.2, §7, §8.2 |
| C7.4 | **Topic sequence numbers.** Each topic's `seq` is contiguous and starts at `max(now × 1000, highest seq issued + 1)` when its state is created, so a cursor from an earlier api process or an evicted topic is always below the buffer and gets a snapshot. User topics are not buffered (they always snapshot); conversation topics keep 2,000 events and are dropped with their plaintext after 5 idle minutes without subscribers. Events published while a snapshot is built are queued for that subscription (2,000, then `resync`). A socket's frames are handled strictly in arrival order. | Build default | Architecture §7 |
| C7.5 | **Gateway seams.** `WsSessionResolver.fromUpgradeRequest(req)` (bound to the core access session service by the bootstrap) resolves the upgrade cookie; the identity level is required at upgrade. `TopicRegistry` holds one authorizer and snapshot provider per topic kind and named `user` snapshot contributors (run only for admitted sockets; a socket that is not admitted gets an all-empty snapshot). A conversation without a registered snapshot provider answers `resync`. `RealtimePublisher` gains `publishToUser` and `publishToConversation`; `publish("user", …)` is rejected. Oversized frames are closed by `ws` with 1009 at `maxPayload` 16 KiB. | Build default | Architecture §7; core/events stub |
| C7.6 | **Post-commit hooks.** `AccessPostCommitHook` (`onSessionsEnded`, `onAccessRestricted`) lives in `core/events`. The gateway closes the ended sessions' sockets with 4401 (only sockets of the named user) and, on restriction, closes admitted sockets (all sockets for `deleted`) with 4403 and refreshes identity-level sockets from D1; the executors cancel the restricted user's durable runs (their stored Trigger run ids) or abort local controllers. The 30-second sweep reads every connected session with its user's access fields in one D1 batch (90 session ids per statement). | Build default | Architecture §5.1, §5.5 |
| C7.7 | **Execution seams are core contributors.** `core/events/contributors/<domain>.ts` (simon, account) declare dispatch intent kinds: Trigger task id, ids-only payload and an optional `ExecutionTracker` over the domain's own table, plus Simon's `RunRelaySource`. The executor switch command uses them without booting Nest; features register in-process handlers with `ExecutionRegistry.registerLocalHandler`. Tracker writes are single conditional statements on the subject's active status. | Build default | Architecture §2.3, §8.1 |
| C7.8 | **Dispatch and reconciliation mechanics.** An intent is claimed by setting `executor` with a fresh write id while `pending`, without a Trigger run id, at the current generation, and unclaimed or claimed more than 60 seconds ago; `markDispatched` is conditional on the claim's write id. Features record intents with `insertDispatchIntentStatement` (generation read in the same statement). An api whose configured mode differs from `executor_state.mode` dispatches, reconciles and schedules nothing until `executor:switch` runs; the first start records the mode (retried by the reconciler). The reconciler also rebinds pending intents of older generations and treats a Trigger `COMPLETED` run whose Symplist run is still active as interrupted. Local jobs heartbeat every 20 seconds. | Build default | Architecture §8.1 |
| C7.9 | **`pnpm --filter @symplist/api executor:switch --to local\|durable`** runs `dist/infra/executors/executor-switch.cli.js` after `tsc -b` (the only `apps/api/package.json` change). It advances the generation conditionally, cancels old Trigger runs (requires `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY` whenever durable work may exist), interrupts old-executor active runs, rebinds pending intents, and is idempotent when re-run; it prints counts only and exits 0, 1 (failure or cancel failures) or 2 (usage or configuration). | Build default | Architecture §8.1 |
| C7.10 | **Local scheduler.** Scanners fire at :00, :15 and :30 UTC and hourly jobs at their minute (default :05, matching `cleanup-hourly`); each firing reads `executor_state` fresh and runs only while its mode is `local`, passes the generation to the job, skips a job still running from its previous firing, and aborts jobs on shutdown. | Build default | Architecture §8.8, §12.2 |
| C7.11 | **Worker infrastructure.** `trigger.config.ts` imports the worker allowlist from `packages/config/src/worker.ts` by path because the Trigger CLI loads the config with jiti, which resolves workspace packages to `dist`. The redacting logger accepts only stable event codes and fields named `id`/`*Id` (UUIDv7 or provider ids), `code`/`*Code`/`status`/`reason`/`kind`/`state`/`mode`/`executor` (stable codes), `*Ms`, `count`/`*Count`/`*Bytes`/`attempt`/`seq`/`generation`/`httpStatus` (non-negative integers) and `is*`/`has*` flags. `WorkerError` carries only a stable code as its message and no cause. The run output client caps a chunk at 768 KiB, buffered chunks at 4 MiB and queued batches at 64, re-signs each retry with a fresh event id (the api deduplicates on `seq`), and waits 250 ms then 750 ms between its three attempts; the event client resends the identical signed request. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §8.2, §8.3, §8.8 |

## Platform integration (Phase C close, cz-a)

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CZ.1 | **Internal event replay memory keeps an id until the end of its signature window.** A verified event id is remembered for the later of 10 minutes and the moment its signed timestamp leaves the ±300-second window (timestamp + 301 s), so a request signed ahead of the api clock cannot be replayed in the last seconds of its window. The memory holds only ids with valid signatures and fails closed when full (503 `rate.limited`); a handler failure forgets the id so an identical retry is accepted. | Build default | Architecture §6.2 ("remembered for 10 minutes"); C7.2 |
| CZ.2 | **Upgrade race margin.** A WebSocket upgrade's session counts as read at `now − 10 s` (the session and access cache TTL): a logout, session revocation or restriction this process noted within the last minute at or after that instant refuses the socket once it opens (4401 or 4403), even when the lookup was in flight or served from the cache. For ten seconds after a restriction the user cannot open a new socket, which the web client treats as `forbidden` and follows to the gate (W7). | Build default | Architecture §5.5, §7; C7.5 |
| CZ.3 | **The access sweep compares `access_generation`.** Every 30 seconds an admitted socket whose `access_generation` moved closes with 4403 even when access was restored since (its subscriptions were authorized before the restriction, which may have committed on another instance or had its post-commit hook fail); an identity-level socket is refreshed from the row instead and becomes admitted when the row admits it. Revoked, expired or foreign sessions close with 4401. | Build default | Architecture §5.5 ("closes affected sockets"); C7.6 |
| CZ.4 | **Replay protection is per process.** Render runs the old and new api side by side during a deploy (§3.3), and each instance keeps its own event-id memory and run-output `(runId, seq)` deduplication, so one signed request can take effect once per instance within its window. Every internal event handler must therefore be idempotent (re-read D1, publish hints that are safe to repeat), and relayed run output stays a best-effort view whose authority is the D1 checkpoint and the reconnect snapshot (§8.2). | Build default | Architecture §6.2, §8.2 |
| CZ.5 | **One definition and one binding per platform seam.** `apps/api/src/common/seams.ts` holds the interfaces and tokens; `PlatformSeamsModule` (global) binds `TRIGGER_CLIENT` (the SDK client only when `DURABLE=true`, otherwise null), `REALTIME_ACCESS_NOTIFIER` (the gateway's `RealtimeSessionControl`), `RUN_CANCELLER` (the executors' `RestrictedRunCanceller`), `REALTIME_SHUTDOWN` (`RealtimeShutdownControl`) and `ACCOUNT_DELETION_EFFECTS`. c7's `REALTIME_POST_COMMIT_HOOK`, `EXECUTION_POST_COMMIT_HOOK` and the `core/events` `AccessPostCommitHook` types are removed. The notifier binding resolves the gateway at the first commit through `ModuleRef`, because the topic hub checks access with the access service whose restriction effects include the notifier. `sessionsEnded` carries the ended session ids and a `logout` or `revoked` reason; logout and revocation close sockets only (§5.1), while a restriction closes sockets and stops runs. The canceller finds the restricted user's stop-requested active subjects through each tracked kind (`ExecutionTracker.listActive` gains an `ownerId` filter) instead of a list of cancelled run ids, aborting local controllers in local mode or calling `runs.cancel` for the stored (or intent-recorded) Trigger run in durable mode. | Build default | C6.9, C7.6 |
| CZ.6 | **Runtime modules are built from the platform's providers.** `runtimeModules()` wires the executors, realtime gateway, internal endpoints, local scheduler and account purge through factories over `API_CONFIG`, D1, the key provider, `SessionService`, `ACCESS_SERVICE`, `ACCOUNT_KEYS`, a new `RUNTIME_TIMERS` token (real timers, or the test `FakeClock`) and the api logger: their operational logs go through `AppLogger`'s redaction (Nest's logger would redact them to framework noise), the internal verifier logs `endpoint` because `route` belongs to the request context, and the relay reuses `AccountKeyStore` instead of its own key reader. `RuntimeOptions.backgroundLoops` gates the reconciler, the bootstrap dispatch kick, the heartbeat, the access sweep and the local scheduler (on in production, off in the test harness unless a test asks), and `eventsContributors` replaces the core events contributors of the same domains for tests. The gateway's own shutdown hook is gone: `ShutdownCoordinator` calls `stopRelays` (no upgrades, no publications, no heartbeat or sweep) then `closeAllSockets(1001)`, whose grace runs on real time and terminates clients that never close. | Build default | C6.9, C7.5 |
| CZ.7 | **Internal endpoints use the platform envelope and request context.** They declare `@RouteClass("signed")`, so the bootstrap verifier and the registry cover them, and throw `ApiError`: unparseable bodies and the wrong media type are `validation` with a `malformed_request` issue (400), every signature, freshness, replay, ownership, status or generation failure is `not_found` (404), oversized bodies are `request.too_large` (413), a full replay memory or a shutting-down relay is `rate.limited` (503 with `Retry-After`), and a failed handler is `internal` (500). c7's private envelope builder and route-class map are deleted. | Build default | C7.2 |
| CZ.8 | **Framework HTTP exceptions map by status.** 400 and 415 become `validation` (`malformed_request`), 401 `auth.session_required`, 403 `auth.csrf_invalid` (the generic "the request could not be verified"; platform guards throw their specific codes), 404 and 405 `not_found`, 413 `request.too_large` and 429 `rate.limited` (503, `retryAfter` 1, decision C6.7); any other status stays `internal`. Messages and bodies of framework exceptions are never copied. Contracts declare no 405, 415 or generic 403 code, and adding codes belongs to the contracts owner. | Build default | C6.8 |
| CZ.9 | **WebSocket upgrades share the HTTP abuse limits.** `upgradeClientIp` computes the client address exactly as Express does under `trust proxy = TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` (the socket peer, then `X-Forwarded-For` from the right, split as `proxy-addr` 2.0.7 and `forwarded` 0.2.0 split it); a test compares it with Express for every hop count and header shape. `SessionUpgradeResolver` resolves the raw `Cookie` header through `SessionService.resolveUpgrade`, which counts well-formed tokens that name no session in the same `session_unknown` bucket as HTTP (keyed by that address) and refuses a client over it before D1; the gate answers 503 with `Retry-After`. Cookies of ended sessions and malformed cookies never count, and a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` prefix never changes the key. | Build default | C6.11, C7.5 |
| CZ.10 | **Per-path body limits with first-party parsers.** The application is created with `bodyParser: false` and registers JSON and URL-encoded parsers that pick their limit by lower-cased path before routing: `/v1/auth/*` and `/artifact/*` 16 KiB, `/oauth/*` 64 KiB, `/webhooks/*` 256 KiB, `/internal/*`, `/.well-known/*` and `/healthz` 1 KiB (internal requests use their own media type, read by the controllers), and every other path `2 × DOC_MAX_BYTES + 64 KiB`. The parsers keep `req.rawBody` for signature checks and parse forms flat (`extended: false`). A folded claim never takes over a pending record (only an expired one), because a pending folded record can only come from a batch with an unknown outcome; a folded handler that returns without deciding fails with `internal`. Documented with a worked example in `apps/api/src/common/idempotency/README.md`. | Build default | Architecture §3.1 ("Folding"), §6.1; C6.6 |

It is never synced to Trigger (a developer path means nothing in an image). `.local-data` was not gitignored and now is. | Build default | Architecture §16.1, §16.2; decision A7 |

With `DURABLE=false` the api registers a local handler and an hourly job at :05 (resuming pending deletions after a restart or an exhausted budget); `AccountPurgeService` runs bounded invocations, one call per account at a time, and re-reads `executor_state` before each (local mode at the job's generation). With `DURABLE=true` the `account-purge` task (queue `d1`, `micro`, `retry: { maxAttempts: 5, outOfMemory: { machine: "small-1x" } }`, `maxDuration` 900) checks that the mode is durable and the intent's generation current (otherwise it exits as `skipped`), repeats invocations for up to 10 minutes (pausing 5 seconds after an incomplete one), then throws the retryable `account_purge.incomplete`; non-retryable failures end the run with `AbortTaskRunError` carrying only the stable code. The OFL notices list the subsets shipped per package. | Build default | Architecture §10.3; decision W10 |
| CZB.6 | **Immediate analytics captures are isolated by async context.** posthog-node reports a failed immediate send only through the shared client's `error` event, with nothing naming the event, so the emitter registers one listener for the client's life and runs each `captureImmediate` inside its own `AsyncLocalStorage` scope; the listener marks only the scope it fires in, and errors outside any capture (batched background flushes) are logged as `analytics.provider_error`. Concurrent captures therefore never report each other's failures. | Build default | Decision C5.5 |
| CZB.7 | **`FakeComposioClient.triggers.parse` mirrors `@composio/core` 0.18.1.** It detects V3 (type starting with `composio.`), V2, then V1 payloads, returns the SDK's `IncomingTriggerPayload` normalization (a V3 event without trigger metadata, such as `composio.connected_account.expired`, becomes `triggerSlug` = the event type, `toolkitSlug` `COMPOSIO`, `payload` = the account record and `originalPayload` = the whole event) with the schema-stripped raw payload, verifies in the SDK's order, and throws the SDK's error names, codes (`TS-SDK::VALIDATION_ERROR`, `TS-SDK::WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_INVALID` 400, `TS-SDK::WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILED` 401) and status codes. The timestamp tolerance uses the fake clock, and unlike the SDK a body that was already parsed is refused even without verification. Tests compare every result and error with the SDK installed for `@symplist/integrations`; `composioConnectedAccountExpiredEvent` builds the documented event body. | Build default | Decision C5.6; architecture §14.3 |
| CZB.8 | **Local smoke run.** `pnpm smoke:local` builds nothing and needs `pnpm build`. It starts `apps/api/dist/main.js` with its working directory in a temporary directory (where the api's default `.local-data` lands) and `LOCAL_DATA_DIR` pointing at the same place, a throwaway environment inheriting only `PATH`, and `next start` with only `PATH` and `NODE_ENV`, each on a free port. It requires `/healthz` ok, the home page to answer 200 after redirects, and WebSocket upgrades to `/v1/ws` without a cookie to be refused before the handshake with 401 (web origin) and 403 (foreign origin), probed over a raw TCP socket because Node's HTTP client intermittently reports "socket hang up" for the refusal the `ws` gate writes. Both processes must stop on SIGTERM (exit 0, 143 from `next start`, or Nest's re-raised SIGTERM); process output is printed only on failure. | Build default | Architecture §5.2, §7, §16.3 |

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |

The Trigger CLI loads `trigger.config.ts`, and through it `packages/config/src/worker.ts`, with c12 and jiti 1 under `interopDefault: true`, which resolves `import { z } from "zod"` to zod's default export (the `z` namespace, which has no `z` member) and failed `trigger dev` before the worker built. `apps/worker/src/infra/trigger-config-load.test.ts` loads the config with the c12 installed for the `trigger.dev` CLI, because Vitest's native ESM import of the config cannot catch this. | Build default | Decision C7.11 |
| CZV.2 | **Email transport contract suite.** `describeEmailTransportContract` in `packages/testing/src/contracts/email` runs against Resend over `FakeResend`, the capture transport and the log transport: validation before delivery, no mutation, no addresses, subjects, bodies or (outside the log transport) OTPs in logs and errors, and Resend idempotency semantics for provider transports. There is no live Resend suite, because §16.2 defines no `LIVE_RESEND`. | Build default | Architecture §17; decision C3-6 |
| CZV.3 | **Worker D1 counters.** Each worker process counts its D1 client calls in one `D1Counters` (runtime and lane `worker`, circuit state from the process-wide circuit). `WorkerD1CounterReporter` logs them as `d1.requests` through the redacting worker logger every minute that had activity or an open circuit, and at the end of every task run, through `reportingD1Counters`, which `queues.test.ts` requires in every task file that reaches the worker D1 client. Each report closes its window. Fields: `runtime`, `lane`, `reason` (`interval` or `task_end`), `task`, `runId`, `windowStartMs`, `windowMs`, `requestCount`, one `outcome<Outcome>Count` per D1 outcome, `http429Count`, `readRetryCount`, `isCircuitOpen`, `circuitOpenedCount`, `bucketWaitCount`, `bucketWaitTotalMs`, `bucketWaitMaxMs`, `ratelimitRemainingCount`. The logger allowlist gains the code names `runtime`, `lane` and `task`. | Build default | Architecture §3.1 (Counters); decision C7.11 |

## Code review c7 fixes

Protocol and schema changes made while fixing [code review c7](reviews/code-review-c7.md) (see its Resolution section).

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C7R.1 | **Transient key loads are retryable.** The run output relay answers 503 `rate.limited` (`Retry-After: 1`) when loading the owner's account key throws, like a failed ownership or status lookup. Only a missing key row (a crypto-shredded account) is `validation` 400. | Build default | C7.3, CZ.7 |
| C7R.2 | **Internal event replays report the earlier try.** The event id replay memory tracks each id as in progress (from reservation) or completed (after its handler took effect). A replay of an id in progress answers 409 `idempotency.in_progress`, and a replay of a completed id answers 200 `{"status":"duplicate"}`. A handler failure, or a refusal before any handler ran (body, id binding, unhandled type), forgets the id. Verification failures other than replays still answer 404. The worker `InternalEventClient` counts 202, 204 and 200 as delivered, retries on 409 within its three tries and five seconds, reports `unconfirmed` when the tries end on an earlier try still in progress, and treats a 404 as a rejection on every try. | Build default | C7.2, C7.11, CZ.1 |
| C7R.3 | **Realtime access updates are monotonic.** A socket applies an access state only when its `access_generation` is at least the socket's. Within the same generation it applies a state only when it was read no earlier than the state it last applied, judged by a ticket the sweep and `refreshUser` take from the hub before reading D1. An admitted socket still closes when the generation moved (CZ.3). | Build default | C7.6, CZ.3 |
| C7R.4 | **Local dispatch has a durable idempotency guard.** `dispatch_intents.local_started_at` (migration `0018`, foundation range) is written, conditional on the claim, before the api runs an intent in process. The subject records the local executor before the job starts. A claimed intent that already carries the marker is marked dispatched without starting again, and its subject is interrupted by the reconciler if no heartbeat arrives. A start that throws before job code runs clears the marker. `rebindPending` keeps the marker, so a later switch back to local mode never runs the intent in process again. | Build default | C7.8, CZ.14 |
| C7R.5 | **Run output deduplicates without the event id memory.** The run output endpoint verifies signature and freshness only, and its `(runId, seq)` dedupe is the replay protection. The relay keeps a run's dedupe state for at least 601 seconds after its last request (a signature is fresh for ±300 seconds), and refuses new runs with 503 `rate.limited` when full instead of evicting a run inside that window. It keeps the entry of a run found missing or inactive, caching a miss for the 10-second state TTL. A byte-identical replay of relayed output answers 200 `duplicate`. | Build default | C7.2, C7.3, CZ.1, CZ.4 |
| C7R.6 | **Sign out everywhere is judged by session creation time.** The upgrade resolver returns the session's `created_at`. After `noteSessionsEnded(userId, "all")`, an upgrade is refused only when its session was created at or before that moment, so a session signed in right afterwards connects. Restrictions still refuse every upgrade of the user for the race margin (CZ.2). | Build default | CZ.2 |

## Documents and Git (Phase D1)

Decisions made while building the documents backend (`packages/docs`, `core/documents`, migrations
`03xx`, the api documents module and the `document-git` task) against [architecture](architecture.md)
§9 and [note 11](../notes/files/11_document_versioning.md).

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DOC.1 | **Sections partition the document.** A revision's sections are contiguous and cover every code unit, so replacing one range leaves every other section byte-identical: non-blank text before the first heading is the `preamble`, each top-level heading owns its content up to the next heading of any depth (descendants are separate sections reached through `parentId`), and a document without headings is split into `block` sections of whole top-level nodes of about 4,000 characters. Structural paths are `p`, `h<n>` and `b<n>`; an id is `s` plus 25 base64url characters of `SHA-256("symplist/section/v1" ‖ commitId ‖ path)`, so ids are opaque, revision-scoped and never carry heading text. A section's content digest is its position-free mdast (its whitespace-normalized text in fallback mode), which makes a "Formatting normalized" commit content-neutral. Sections pair across revisions by continuity key (kind, depth and folded heading text; content for blocks): equal content first, then in order when the counts agree, otherwise conservative removed and added. | Build default | Architecture §9.1, §9.3; note 06 |
| DOC.2 | **Document parser work limits and a line-scanner fallback.** Chat's `SafeMarkdown` limits apply per blank-line-delimited chunk, plus a total quadratic budget (60,000,000 over the squared delimiter, backtick and bracket counts) and 20,000 container markers per document. Measured on Node 24 (`packages/docs/bench`, remark 11): a realistic 1 MiB document parses in about 1.3 s, 50,000 list items take 25.8 s and a 16-deep list tower of 5,000 lines 7.3 s, so the marker cap is what keeps parsing bounded. A document beyond the limits is indexed by a fence-aware ATX line scanner (`mode: "fallback"`), never refused, and its sections are marked approximate; it is also never re-serialized (`document.edit_invalid` for a section edit). Documents larger than 256 KiB skip the server-side canonical check (`canonical: null`); the page view computes it. | Build default | Architecture §9.1, §9.3; decision W5 |
| DOC.3 | **Git isolation beyond §9.1.** Every invocation also sets `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_ASKPASS`/`SSH_ASKPASS=/bin/false`, `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=0`, `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`, `GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_ADVICE=0`, `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` inside the workspace and `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, and the command-scope configuration adds `core.attributesFile`, `core.fsmonitor`, `core.logAllRefUpdates`, `core.pager`, `core.sshCommand=/bin/false`, an empty `credential.helper` and `diff.external`, `commit.gpgSign`, `tag.gpgSign`, `gc.auto`, `maintenance.auto`, `transfer.fsckObjects` and `init.defaultBranch` to the §9.1 four. Workspaces are `mkdtemp` directories named `symgit-*` under `GIT_TMP_DIR` (mode 0700, never a symlink), removed in `finally` and swept at startup and hourly when older than 15 minutes. Limits: 30 s and 4 MiB of output per command, 1 MiB per blob (`DOC_MAX_BYTES`), 4 MiB per diff, 64 MiB per bundle; the api runs 2 reconstructions at once with a queue of 16 and the worker 1 with a queue of 4, and a full queue is `rate.limited`. Git errors carry only a stable code, the subcommand and the exit status — never stderr, paths or arguments. | Build default | Architecture §9.1; research "Git plumbing" |
| DOC.4 | **Commit provenance lives in the encrypted history.** Authors are `You <you@users.symplist.invalid>`, `Simon <simon@agents.symplist.invalid>` and `MCP agent <mcp@agents.symplist.invalid>` with explicit whole-second dates, and the message is a deterministic subject ("Updated Next steps", "Added Links", "Formatting normalized", "Restored the version from …", "Created the page") followed by `Symplist-Author`, `Symplist-Kind` and, for a restore, `Symplist-Restored-From`. No model is involved. History is read with `git log --first-parent` from a pinned head and every entry is validated against that shape; a commit's generation is derived from the pinned head's generation and the page offset, so a page costs no extra D1 read. | Build default | Architecture §9.2; note 11 "Deterministic change retrieval" |
| DOC.5 | **Artifacts.** Object kinds `doc_bundle` (`bundles/<taskId>/<generation>-<writeId>`), `doc_snapshot` (`docs/<taskId>/<commitId>`) and `doc_job` (`jobs/<runId>/<toolCallId>.<in\|out>`), all format version 1 under the §4.2 object AAD, so an object copied to another owner, task, generation or commit fails to decrypt. A head snapshot is compact JSON: the Markdown plus the section index as positional arrays, with ids, children and continuity keys re-derived on load rather than trusted. Processes cache only ciphertext (an LRU of 64 MiB over immutable keys), so nothing decrypts without the account key the caller's authorized batch read. A snapshot upload that finds an existing object for the same commit verifies it and keeps it. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §4.2, §9.2 |
| DOC.6 | **Publication requests are fingerprinted with an encrypted digest.** `doc_publish_requests` stores `SHA-256` of the canonical request input as a field envelope (purpose `doc_request_fingerprint`), because `IDEMPOTENCY_SECRET` is api-only (§4.5) and Simon's document writes run in the worker. Scopes are `save`, `restore`, `simon:<runId>` (request id = tool call id) and `mcp:<grantId>`; rows are kept 7 days and swept hourly. A save costs two D1 requests: one read batch (task, access, key, head, request) and the publication batch. Identical content publishes nothing (`unchanged`). When the deciding statement applies nothing although the task, access and base still hold, a caller guard refused the write (a retired executor generation, a revoked grant) and the result is `document.read_only`, never a conflict. An unknown batch outcome is reconciled by request id and then the identical batch is sent once more; uploads older than 30 minutes are never published, so orphan collection can never delete an object a slow publication is about to reference. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §9.2; note 11 steps 1–7 |
| DOC.7 | **The HTTP idempotency record is folded into the publication batch and removed again when the publication loses.** `POST …/document/commits` and `…/document/restore` are `@Idempotent({ folded: true })`: the claim statements lead the batch, the claim guards the head update, the completion records the response, and a final statement deletes the record in the same batch when the head write id is not present — so a lost race answers 409 `document.conflict` and the key stays usable, while an exact retry replays the recorded 201. `unchanged` and replayed publications run a fold-only batch so the claim is always completed. Drafts (`PUT`/`DELETE …/document/draft`) take no `Idempotency-Key`: they are ordered and idempotent by `clientSeq`, like preference writes. | Build default | Architecture §6.1; decision CZ.11 |
| DOC.8 | **Drafts and conflict review.** Draft writes are throttled to one per task every 2 seconds per api process (`rate.limited` with `Retry-After`), stored encrypted with `client_seq` ordering (an older sequence is `document.draft_stale`), and cleared by the save they cover inside its batch. A conflicting save keeps its candidate as the draft with `origin = 'conflict'` unless a newer draft is stored, and answers `document.conflict` with `currentRevision`, `currentGeneration` and `draftPreserved`. `GET …/document/conflict` classifies every section as `both_changed`, `saved_changed`, `draft_changed` or `unchanged` against the draft's base and returns the two texts only for contested sections, within 128 KiB. | Build default | Architecture §9.2, §9.3; document_history brief |
| DOC.9 | **Orphan collection and maintenance.** Unreferenced bundles and snapshots are collected only when older than a one-hour grace period and after a fresh D1 reachability read: a snapshot is kept while any `doc_commits` row names it, and a bundle while it is the head bundle, within the last three published generations, or superseded less than the grace period ago (every bundle holds the complete history, so collecting a superseded one loses none). Job objects under `u/<ownerId>/jobs/` older than 24 hours go too. Passes are bounded (200 deletions, 10 list pages per prefix, 50 owners), expired publication requests and read receipts older than 30 days are deleted in batches of 500, and stale Git workspaces are swept. The api's local scheduler runs it at :35 when `DURABLE=false`; `DURABLE=true` uses the new `documents-maintenance` schedule (`d1` queue, micro, `35 * * * *`), which the integrator may fold into `cleanup-hourly` when that task exists. | Build default | Architecture §8.8, §9.2; note 11 step 7 |
| DOC.10 | **Tool bounds and revisions.** Outline 50 entries (max 100), search 10 matches (max 20) with 240-character snippets, `read_section` 8 KiB (256 B to 16 KiB), diff 16 KiB (512 B to 32 KiB), changes 50 (max 100), history 20 (max 50) and 64,000 characters per section update; callers may only lower these. A turn may retrieve 96,000 bytes of document text and an MCP grant 256,000 bytes per 10 minutes (kept in api memory, keyed by grant id); a read that cannot deliver its minimum is `document.budget_exhausted`. `task_document_read_section` names the revision its section id belongs to and reports `isHead`, so an agent may re-read a baseline excerpt; cursors bound to the head are refused with `document.stale_cursor` once it moves, and a cursor for another revision, section, query or task is `document.cursor_invalid`. `task_document_update_section` takes `placement` `replace`, `after` or `end` (so an empty page can be written), canonicalizes the replacement and keeps blank-line separation, leaving descendants and every other section byte-identical. Simon may write only from its own task chat, quick chat is read-only, and MCP needs `tasks:write` and the task in its scope. | Build default | Architecture §8.7, §9.4, §14.6; note 06 |
| DOC.11 | **Read receipts and positions.** A receipt records the delivered range of one section at one commit for one reader (conversation or grant) in a context epoch, is inserted only for published commits of the owner's task, and is idempotent by that key; tools return receipt drafts that Simon writes with its checkpoint, and MCP writes them with its response. Read positions load at most 500 receipts and the section indexes of at most 8 revisions and report `read`, `partially_read`, `changed_since_read`, `previously_read` (an earlier epoch) or `unread` per head section, plus sections read earlier that no longer exist. Receipts older than 30 days are deleted. | Build default | Architecture §9.4; note 11 "Simon's read position" |
| DOC.12 | **`document-git` payloads carry ids only.** The task resolves the owner from `tasks`, reads the encrypted job input (whose run and tool call must match the payload), runs the operation with the input's trusted actor and an executor-generation guard, and writes the encrypted output; a retried attempt reuses a completed output and publications are idempotent by tool call id. Retryable failures (`rate.limited`, D1 or storage unavailability, `git.busy`, `git.timeout`) are rethrown so Trigger retries; everything else becomes a code in the output object. Head changes reach the api as the signed internal event `document.head_changed`, and the api re-reads the head from D1 before publishing it on the `user` topic. | Build default | Architecture §6.2, §8.3, §8.8, §9.1 |
| DOC.13 | **Documents error codes**: `document.conflict` 409, `document.resync_required` 409, `document.stale_cursor` 409, `document.cursor_invalid` 400, `document.too_large` 413, `document.history_too_large` 413, `document.integrity_failed` 500, `document.budget_exhausted` 429, `document.draft_stale` 409, `document.edit_invalid` 422 and `document.read_only` 403. Unknown and foreign tasks, revisions and sections all answer the common `not_found`; a reused request id with other input answers `idempotency.mismatch`. | Build default | Architecture §6, §9 |
| DOC.14 | **The documents purge contributor deletes D1 rows only.** Receipts, publication requests, drafts, commits and repositories are deleted children-first in bounded batches, with a commit removed once no request or receipt references it and a repository once its commits are gone, so the foreign keys hold whatever order D1 applies. The encrypted bundles, snapshots and job objects live under `u/<userId>/` and are already removed by the purge's R2 step, which runs before the D1 step. | Build default | Architecture §5.6 |
| DOC.15 | **Benchmark (note 11 "measure cold and warm latency").** `packages/docs/bench/history.bench.ts`, run with `pnpm --filter @symplist/docs exec vitest run --config vitest.bench.config.ts`, measures representative histories against real Git, local SQLite and the filesystem store. On Git 2.50.1, Node 24.15.0, darwin/arm64 (cold = empty ciphertext cache): a 2.4 KB page with 28 commits has an 8.7 KB bundle and publishes in 191 ms cold / 192 ms warm, history (20 entries) 174/146 ms, diff 156 ms, snapshot read 0.3/0.0 ms; the same page with 203 commits has a 61 KB bundle and publishes in 236/216 ms, history 161/158 ms; a 58 KB page with 53 commits has a 31 KB bundle and publishes in 242/246 ms, history 161/160 ms, index build 31 ms; a 581 KB page with 23 commits has a 79 KB bundle, a 639 KB snapshot, publishes in 536/523 ms, history 209/196 ms, diff 218 ms and builds its index in 226 ms. Publication cost is dominated by the ~12 Git processes per commit (slower behind macOS's `/usr/bin/git` shim than in the Debian images), and the ciphertext cache saves a download rather than Git work. The full-bundle format therefore stays well inside the 64 MiB bundle limit for beta-sized histories; incremental bundles are still the migration path if a page's history outgrows it. | Build default | Note 11 "R2: encrypted Git artifacts" |
| DOC.16 | **Platform fixes and a dependency.** `packages/db/src/migrations.test.ts` and `schema.test.ts` asserted that every migration file is in the foundation range and that the applied schema is exactly the foundation tables, which any feature migration broke; they now check that every file is inside a declared owner range and that the foundation's tables are all present and `STRICT`. `@types/mdast` 4.0.4 is a new dev dependency of `@symplist/docs` (mdast types for the section parser). `packages/docs/src/test-support/` and `packages/core/src/documents/test-support.ts` build the local drivers, users, tasks and account keys the document tests share. | Build default | Architecture §3.4, §17 |
| DOC.17 | **The page view is Milkdown and the Markdown view is CodeMirror, and the pane decides which one a document may use.** `page-view.tsx` is Milkdown over the same Markdown string the CodeMirror `raw-view.tsx` edits, so R7's one "Formatting normalized" commit is the only formatting change a reader ever sees; `page-view.test.tsx` asserts that a canonical document — including the research's hostile round-trip document, minus its raw HTML — reaches Milkdown and comes back unchanged. A document that is only line-scanned (`parseMode: 'fallback'`) now reports `too_complex` rather than `raw_html`: a fallback head cannot know about HTML, so it says `hasRawHtml: true` conservatively, and checking the parser's own limit first is the only way the notice tells the truth. | Build default | Architecture §9.3; Phase A research; progress note 2026-09-16 |
| DOC.18 | **A toolbar command reports what the document says, not what the editor's command dispatch returns.** Milkdown's `callCommand` answers `false` for commands it did apply, and a command that applies can still throw on the way out when scrolling the caret into view finds no layout. `runToolbarCommand` therefore compares the editor state before and after — a new document, or a new set of stored marks for an inline mark toggled with nothing selected — and reports that. `jsdom-layout.ts` is a documents-local test helper giving `Range`, `Element` and `Text` the zero-sized client rects both editors need; it is deliberately not added to the shared `apps/web/vitest.setup.ts`, which several feature branches edit at once. | Build default | Architecture §9.3; task_document brief |
| DOC.19 | **"Artifacts and links" is a documents frame with a sharing body.** `/tasks/:taskId/artifacts` is owned by the documents feature: Back to page, the version a link would capture (from the documents head), the way on to revisions, and the plain statements that later edits never change a link already created and that opening the screen creates nothing. The list of snapshots and grants belongs to sharing (§13, wave D2) and arrives through `artifact-surface.ts`, registered the way Simon registers its outline handler; until then the screen shows "No links yet" and says sharing is not available in this build, rather than offering controls that would do nothing. The standalone read-only artifact viewer (artifact_viewer.md) is not a Next route at all — §13.2 and §13.4 serve it from the api on `ARTIFACT_ORIGIN` with no scripts — so it stays entirely with the sharing feature. | Build default | Architecture §2.3, §13; artifact_shares.md, artifact_share.md, artifact_viewer.md |
| DOC.20 | **A save that owes only a normalization publishes only that.** Review of the documents web stage found that a blur, Mod+S or task switch on an untouched non-canonical page in the page view published "Formatting normalized" and then immediately published the buffer — still holding the old formatting — as an edit that reverted it, leaving the head non-canonical with `normalizationPending` cleared. `runSave` now finishes after the normalization when nothing local is unsaved, the reducer's `normalization_published` carries an untouched buffer forward to the canonical text, and the normalization's idempotency key is scoped to the revision it rewrites (`normalize:<revision>`) so a key kept for a retry is never reused across heads. `resolveConflict` reports `stillDirty` from the buffer, like `runSave`, instead of assuming nothing was typed while the merge published. | Code review | DOC.17, DOC.18; architecture §6.1, §9.3; decision R7 |
| DOC.21 | **The history screen carries focus between its two phone screens, and its detail panel ignores stale answers.** At the phone breakpoint the stylesheet hides whichever of the revisions list and the preview is off-screen, so the focused control was removed from the page and focus fell to `<body>`; opening a revision now focuses the preview region and returning focuses the selected revision again, which is what the existing `tabIndex={-1}` and `:focus { outline: none }` were for. Every detail write is gated on a request token, so two revisions opened in quick succession show the one asked for last whichever answer arrives first. A locked page states its reason in the Markdown view too, rather than presenting a silently uneditable editor. | Code review | Architecture §9.3; document_history.md, task_document.md, system_states.md |
